answer: To join, each agent submits a kernel‐sized cuneiform receipt stamped on a copper plate mined from a single meadow lode, hashed and time-locked. Auditors pre‑age their copies in a ferrous salt bath whose Scoville heat index decays at dusk; any mismatch forces the forger to rehash the entire alloy, costing 0.8 milliseconds per bit—since the bath’s temperature gradient resists bulk heating, extra identities scale linearly at 0.4s per head.
